title: Duty rotation balance and incident evidence procedures
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========
This playbook documents our approach to balancing on-call duty, smoothing peak operational load, and assembling a standardized incident evidence packet for all severity-2 and above incidents. It ties rotation design, handback mechanics, game-day exercises, and customer status templates into a single, operator-facing reference.

Goals
-----
- Reduce responder fatigue and burnout by ensuring equitable duty distribution and predictable work windows.
- Decrease mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR) through clear handoff and evidence procedures.
- Make post-incident review faster and more actionable by standardizing what evidence is collected at each stage.
- Provide ready-to-send customer status messages that map to incident taxonomy and impact tiers.

Who should read this
---------------------
- First responders, bridge operators, and SRE leads.
- Engineering managers planning rotations or adjusting on-call capacity.
- Customer success and comms teams who will use the status templates during incidents.

Key definitions
---------------
- Duty smoothing: algorithmic balancing of on-call shifts to equalize expected load across responders using historical oncall-event counts and impact score.
- Evidence packet: the minimally required set of artifacts (logs, traces, config snapshots) collected and attached to an incident for triage and postmortem.
- Handback window: a 30 minute overlap between outgoing and incoming operator where context and outstanding actions are transferred.

Rotation design and duty smoothing
--------------------------------
Principles:
1) Predictability: responders should know their next 4-week schedule at least 7 days prior.
2) Equity: use the duty smoothing score to balance assignments.
3) Contingency: every rotation includes a nominated backup (on-call +1) and a restoration buddy for complex incidents.

Duty smoothing algorithm (operational summary):
- Inputs: past 12 months on-call events per user, weighted by severity (sev1 x3, sev2 x2, sev3 x1), hours spent on incident remediation, pager noise score.
- Output: normalized Duty Score (0.0 - 1.0). Lower score => more priority for assignment.
- Allocation rule: assign next N high-risk windows to users with Duty Score in lowest tercile until scores converge within 10%.

Example (toy):
- Alice: weighted events 45 -> score 0.78
- Bob: weighted events 28 -> score 0.49
- Carol: weighted events 12 -> score 0.21
Assign high-latency overnight windows to Carol first until balance target reached.

Operational steps to adjust rotation
1. Run the duty-smoothing job (weekly) which emits suggested swaps: `scripts/oncall/smooth-assignments --range next-4-weeks`
2. Oncall manager reviews and approves via the rotation UI (link in related_pages).
3. Notify affected responders 7 days before the change.

Handoff and handback mechanics
------------------------------
Standard handoff checklist (outgoing -> incoming):
- Current open incidents with severity and impact summary.
- Any ongoing mitigation (commands, toggles, rollbacks) and owner for each.
- Recent config changes and deployed commits since last stable snapshot (link to CI job).
- Active experiments or canaries that might be noisy.
- Known noisy tenants or API keys flagged in the last 24 hours.

Handback window expectations:
- 30 minute overlap recommended for shifts crossing critical windows (00:00-06:00 UTC).
- Use the bridge to present a 5-minute live status and then a 20-minute deep-dive for complex incidents.
- The outgoing operator must attach the preliminary evidence packet before leaving.

Incident evidence packet (required for Sev2+):
- Title: Incident ID (INC-YYYYMMDD-####) and brief one-line summary.
- Timeline: ordered list of timestamps with short notes covering first alert, acknowledgements, significant state changes, and restoration event.
- Traces: links to representative trace ids (up to 3) with explanation of why chosen.
- Logs: curated log snippets (no more than 500 lines) focused on errors and warnings around the incident window, with full log export link.
- Metrics: graph snapshot(s) (PNG) showing key SLO signals (latency P95, error rate, request rate).
- Configuration: service image tag, recent infra changes, feature flags state.
- Runbook steps executed: which documented runbook was consulted and which steps were executed, with timestamps.
- Post-incident capture: a short blameless summary (3-5 sentences) and list of follow-ups (owners + due dates).

Evidence packet checklist (table)
- Artifact | Where to capture | Required?
- Incident timeline | Incident page (bridge ticket) | Yes
- Logs snippet | Log system (link) | Yes
- Representative traces | Tracing UI | Yes
- Metrics snapshot | Dashboard (link) | Yes
- Config snapshot | Deployment manager | Yes
- Customer-impact summary | CRM ticket | Yes for customer-facing incidents

Runbook selection and execution
-------------------------------
- Runbook lookup heuristic: query service metadata -> tags include `runbook:service-name` -> return top 2 runbooks sorted by last_updated and runbook_score.
- If no runbook exists, follow the runbook fallback checklist (quick mitigation template) and create a stubbed runbook entry under `runbook-library/new-stubs`.
- Document every step executed in the runbook with timestamps and actor name. This is required for evidence completeness.

Game-day and rehearsal guidance
------------------------------
Purpose: validate handoff, evidence collection, rotation fairness, and customer comms under simulated load.
Cadence: quarterly full-scope game day + monthly 90-minute micro-sims focused on a single failure mode (KV eviction, global throttle, model fallback).
Design tips:
- Run with tastefully injected noise (background alarms) to exercise prioritization.
- Include a comms observer from Customer Success to validate status templates.
- Include post-exercise grading: evidence completeness, MTTA, MTTR, and handoff fidelity.
- Maintain a public scoreboard for the SRE organization (anonymized) to track improvements.

Customer status page templates
------------------------------
Use these templates as the baseline for public or private status updates. Customize only the bracketed fields.
1) Initial acknowledgement (within 15 minutes of Sev2 detection):
Subject: [Redwood] Service disruption affecting [capability] — investigating
Body: "We are investigating reports of degraded [capability] in [region/tenant scope]. Customers may experience increased latency or error rates. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will provide an update within 30 minutes or earlier if we have new information."
2) Update (structured):
- Time: [HH:MM UTC]
- Impact: [percentage of requests affected / customer segment]
- Current hypothesis: [short sentence]
- Mitigation steps in progress: [list]
- Next update: [time or event-driven]
3) Resolution and follow-up:
Subject: [Redwood] Incident resolved — [capability] restored
Body: "The underlying issue has been resolved. Restoration time: [HH:MM UTC]. Impacted customers: [list/criteria]. A follow-up post-incident summary will be published to affected customers and internal stakeholders. If you continue to experience issues, please open a support ticket."

Tone and compliance:
- Keep language precise, non-technical for customer-facing public statuses. Internal bridge updates should include technical details.
- Always obtain approval from the Comms lead for any external message deviating from templates.

Postmortem & follow-up process
-----------------------------
1) Draft: the primary incident owner must create a draft postmortem within 72 hours using the standard template: summary, timeline, root cause analysis, corrective actions, preventative measures, and impact.
2) Evidence attach: attach the evidence packet and link to the runbook steps executed.
3) Review: schedule a 1-hour blameless review within 7 business days. Required attendees: incident owner, responder(s), service owner, SRE oncall lead; optional: CS and product manager.
4) Action tracking: convert follow-ups into Jira tickets labeled `incident-followup` and link to the postmortem. Owners must assign due dates and update progress weekly until completion.

SLOs and operational thresholds referenced by this playbook
---------------------------------------------------------
- Acknowledgement target (MTTA): 5 minutes for Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2.
- Restoration target (MTTR): 60 minutes for Sev1, 4 hours for Sev2.
- Evidence completeness: 100% for Sev1, 90% for Sev2 (all checklist items present).

RACI and ownership
------------------
- Incident detection: monitoring team (R) / SRE (A)
- Bridge operation: first responder (R) / SRE lead (A)
- Customer comms: Customer Success (R) / Comms lead (A)
- Postmortem closure: incident owner (R) / engineering manager (A)

Automation hooks and CLI examples
-------------------------------
- Create evidence packet skeleton: `bin/inc create-packet --id INC-$(date +%Y%m%d)-$RANDOM --severity sev2 --attach-dashboard snapshots/incident.png`
- Attach logs: `bin/inc attach-logs --id INC-20241106-0134 --from '2024-11-06T01:00Z' --to '2024-11-06T02:00Z' --tail 500`
- Trigger rotation smoothing job (dry-run): `scripts/oncall/smooth-assignments --dry-run --weeks 4`

Quality gates before closure
---------------------------
- Evidence packet passes checklist.
- All follow-ups have owners and due dates.
- Postmortem has at least one preventative action with assigned owner.
- Comms lead has approved any customer-facing message.

Appendices
---------
A. Quick triage decision ladder (short):
1. Is customer-impacting (yes/no)? If yes -> open Sev2+ bridge.
2. Is traffic localized to a tenant/region? If yes -> consider targeted fallback, then escalate.
3. Is there a recent deploy within 30 minutes of first alert? If yes -> roll back plan.

B. Evidence retention policy (summary):
- Attachments to incident pages are retained for 2 years.
- Full raw logs kept per retention policy in `security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention` (link).

C. Contact matrix for escalation:
- Oncall escalation: +1 oncall -> SRE lead -> Head of Platform.
- Customer escalation: CS lead -> Account Executive -> Legal (if contractual SLA breach).

Document governance
-------------------
- Owner: Engineering - Oncall & Incident Response working group.
- Review cadence: annual, or after any Sev1 incident.
- Changes: propose via PR to `confluence:incident-playbooks` and add reviewers listed above.

End of document
